resources.string: RTK fix lost or corrections stopped

Sound, vibration and a notification (also with the screen off) when the fix falls below the chosen level for 3 s, or the corrections stop arriving, and a short tone when it is back. It only starts warning once that level has been reached.
Android apps that declare and are granted the permission com.PocketGNSS.permission.POSITION receive com.PocketGNSS.action.POSITION up to 5 times a second.
Your own programs (Android apps, MATLAB, Python on a laptop on the hotspot) can read the position without parsing NMEA. See docs/app-interface.md for the fields and examples.

What the app did and what went wrong: connections, correction streams, the phone RTK engine, the screen turning off and on, crashes and why the app last ended. Kept on this phone across restarts; share it to report a problem. It contains no passwords and no positions.
Off: nothing new is written to the log (crashes still are). The entries below stay until cleared.
Bluetooth is off: tap Retry to switch it on

Other devices (laptop, tablet, field controller, another phone) use this phone like a Bluetooth GNSS receiver: they pair with it and read the position as NMEA over a Bluetooth serial port. They get whatever this app computes from the current source: the RFSAT receiver, any external receiver, or Phone RTK, including fix type (RTK fixed / float), accuracy (GST) and correction age.
Use this phone as a high-precision GNSS receiver for other devices over Bluetooth. Set it up once; afterwards one tap switches it on.
Ready: tap On to share the position over Bluetooth.
Bluetooth permission is needed to share the position
No position yet: nothing is sent until there is a fix
No position source connected: connect the receiver or the phone first

Pairing: tap Make visible for pairing (or Pair in Android settings), then on the other device search for Bluetooth devices and pair with this phone. Windows: Settings > Bluetooth > Add device; then More Bluetooth settings > COM Ports shows an Outgoing port for \"PocketGNSS NMEA\": select that COM port in the GNSS / GIS software (any baud rate). Android tablets and field controllers: choose this phone as the external Bluetooth GNSS receiver. Keeps running with the screen off.
Waiting for a device: pair it with \"%1$s\", then connect it to the \"PocketGNSS NMEA\" serial port

Other receivers on the same Wi-Fi or on this phone\'s hotspot (a second tractor, a drone base, a survey rover) connect to the phone as to any NTRIP caster and get the corrections the phone receives. The phone\'s NTRIP relay must be on.
No corrections to relay: switch NTRIP on (Live) with a caster profile.

Check your correction service\'s terms first: many subscriptions allow one rover per account. Relaying a network (VRS) stream gives the other rovers corrections computed for this phone\'s position, good only nearby.
Bluetooth is off. Turn it on and tap Connect.
Choose the receiver\'s Bluetooth device in Setup
Location access is needed to use the phone\'s GNSS
More than 50 km from the base: RTK accuracy degrades. Pick a closer mountpoint or a network (VRS) one.

Three routes bring corrections to the receiver: its own NTRIP client over the mobile network (LTE version) or over Wi-Fi (both versions), set in Tools > Receiver settings (sections 4 and 7); or this relay: the phone fetches RTCM over its mobile data and forwards it to the receiver over Bluetooth or USB, sending the receiver\'s GGA to the caster. The relay also serves other RTCM 3 receivers connected over USB or Bluetooth.

Downloads the caster\'s sourcetable (caster and port from Setup). Network streams are listed first, then single stations nearest first. Tap one to select it; the GGA setting follows the sourcetable. GGA = the caster needs your position (VRS, MAX, nearest base).
Easting and northing are shown on Live and Survey and added to the points CSV. ETRS89 / UTM is the EU-wide grid and the national grid in many Member States; the others are national grids on ETRS89.
Keep the screen on while connected

Some casters send satellite orbits (broadcast ephemerides) only every few minutes, so phone RTK waits. A second connection to an ephemeris stream (BKG\'s BCEP00BKG0 on igs-ip.net, free with BKG registration) gives them at once.
Save the account first: Tools > Corrections > caster profile (e.g. the IGS-IP (BKG) preset with your BKG login).

Not connected: this is the account of the main NTRIP stream, and casters such as Galileo HAS and Metrica allow one login per account (the main stream would stall). Galileo HAS sends its ephemerides in the main stream; otherwise use another account, e.g. BKG\'s BCEP00BKG0.
The receiver link, corrections and outputs are closed.
Edges of this boundary cross each other: the area is not reliable.
Stand on each corner in turn and tap Add corner; the fixes of a few seconds are averaged. Straight edges need only their two ends.

Go round the field along its edge with the antenna; a vertex is added every few metres. At sharp corners tap Add vertex; pause while going round an obstacle. Finish near the start: the boundary closes itself.
A boundary needs at least 3 vertices.
No usable fix of the chosen quality yet.
No fields yet: capture one above or import boundaries (KML, GeoJSON, zipped shapefile).
Paused: no vertices are added while moving.
Same reference frame as the position: ETRS89 with corrections from a European RTK network, WGS 84 / ITRF without them (about 0.9 m apart in Europe).
The datum shift to %1$s is good to about 1 m only; use it for orientation, not for survey work.
Outside the area of %1$s: distortion grows, check the grid choice.
The worked area, overlaps and field coverage recorded so far are deleted.
Drive the first pass along the curve: the passes then follow it, one implement width apart, on both sides. A point is kept every 0.5 m and the path is smoothed to 5 cm. Name and width as above.
Drive at least 10 m before finishing the curve.
Passes round a field boundary, inside it: the first half the implement width in from the boundary, each next one a width further in. Width as above.
Drive the first pass: set A at its start and B at its end (or take them from saved / imported points, or give A and a bearing). The passes then run parallel, one implement width apart, on both sides.
No field boundary here: record or import one (Tools > Field boundary) to see the field\'s coverage and gaps.
No field boundaries yet: record or import one in Tools > Field boundary.
Paints the worked strip (the implement width) on the map. Pause it while the implement is lifted: headland turns, transport.
Shift moves all passes sideways (as seen in the direction of travel), e.g. to match last year\'s tramlines.
A and B are less than 5 m apart: the line direction would be uncertain.
Choose the height model of the country you work in.

Heights in your country\'s height system, from the official geoid model of its mapping agency (published in PROJ-data). It is downloaded once and checked; then it works offline. Heights are right for positions in ETRS89, as given by European RTK networks and by PocketGNSS PPP.
Download the height model in Setup > Display.
Choose a height model in Setup > Display.
Outside %1$s: choose another height model in Setup > Display.
EGM2008 is the best free choice where there is no open national model (for example Greece, Italy, Croatia, Romania); it may differ from national heights by a few decimetres.

Bluetooth Classic (SPP), as the receiver\'s adapter uses; BLE is not used. The receiver sends the same NMEA as over USB. Pair the phone with its adapter (BTU-ESPrtk : <ID>) in Android settings, then choose it below.

The phone\'s own GNSS chip, without an external receiver. With Phone RTK (Setup) its raw measurements are combined with a caster\'s corrections through the NTRIP relay; how close it gets depends on the phone (decimetres to centimetres with carrier phase on L1 + L5). Without corrections, or with Phone RTK off: metre level. Needs location access and location turned on.
A simulated RTK receiver: every screen and tool works without hardware.
NMEA over TCP from the receiver\'s Wi-Fi stream or another relay (for example EOS Tools Pro on port 3967).
Connect the receiver\'s upper micro-USB port (data / COM port, NMEA at 115200 bd) with an OTG cable; the middle port is for power. The app opens automatically when it is plugged in.

Every position the source computes, with the method (for phone RTK: RTK fixed / float, code DGNSS, single, or Android\'s own location) and the accuracy it reported. Offsets are east / north from the reference: by default the mean of the best method present, or the current position (Reference here) – best on a known, still point.
Engine: n = satellites in the solution, φ = signals with carrier phase, r = ambiguity ratio (a fix needs about 3 or more).
Log every position to a CSV file
Saved under Log > Sessions (\"Position history\"), with all columns including the engine\'s internals.

Reported = mean accuracy the method claimed (1 sigma). Actual = RMS distance from the reference. Precision = RMS around the method\'s own mean. Within 2σ = share of positions no further from the reference than twice their reported accuracy: well below 95 % means the method is over-optimistic (or the reference is off).

PocketGNSS manages RFSAT\'s centimetre-accuracy GNSS receiver, developed in the AgriBIT project: a u-blox ZED-F9P / ZED-F9R multi-band receiver with an ESP32 running the ESPrtk firmware and an optional LTE modem. It shows the position and RTK status in real time, over USB or Bluetooth, and lets you configure the receiver.

With RTK corrections, from the receiver\'s own NTRIP client or from the phone, the position reaches 1–2 cm. The app records and exports tracks and surveyed points, averages points with accuracy statistics, stakes out, measures time to fix and can publish the RTK position to other apps on the phone.
Developed with support from Claude AI (Anthropic).
RTKLIB demo5 (T. Takasu, rtklibexplorer; BSD-2), usb-serial-for-android (MIT), MapLibre (BSD), OpenStreetMap, Esri, OpenTopoMap
u-blox ZED-F9P / F9R, ESP32 (ESPrtk), Quectel BG95 LTE, L1/L2/L5
USB-OTG serial, Bluetooth SPP, TCP, NTRIP, UBX
u-blox, ZED-F9P and u-center are trademarks of u-blox AG; ESPrtk of its developers. RFSAT Limited is not affiliated with them.
RFSAT Limited is a non-profit R&D company in Dublin and Athens working on satellite navigation, sensing and signal processing for agriculture, environment and safety.
This file could not be read (CSV, GeoJSON, KML, GPX or zipped shapefile).

CSV (latitude / longitude, or easting / northing in the grid chosen in Setup > Display), GeoJSON, KML, GPX waypoints or a zipped shapefile (.shp, .dbf, .prj). Points are ready for stake-out; boundaries join the field list.
The file has grid coordinates: choose its grid in Setup > Display (for UTM a fixed zone, or connect for the current zone) and import again.
No points or boundaries found in this file.

TASKDATA.zip (ISO 11783-10, version 4.3) with all fields, guidance lines (A-B, curves, headlands) and points, for tractor terminals and farm management software. Unzip it to a USB stick so that the TASKDATA folder is at the top.
No satellite data: enable GSV (Tools > NMEA output) to see the sky plot and signal levels.
off (the receiver uses its own NTRIP client)
Without Wi-Fi or a SIM at the receiver, the phone can relay the corrections: choose a caster profile in Setup > NTRIP relay, then switch NTRIP on (it lists the mountpoints first if none is chosen).
Phone GNSS with Phone RTK off (Setup): corrections are not applied, so the position stays autonomous.
Coordinates in ETRS89 (ETRF2000), converted from the corrections\' global frame (ITRF2020), as European RTK networks and national grids use them.
Coordinates in ITRF2020 at today\'s date, the global frame of the corrections.
Switch the NTRIP relay on with a Galileo HAS or IGS SSRA… stream (caster in Setup > NTRIP relay); until then the phone gives a standalone position.
No second frequency at the moment (too few satellites with L1 + L5 carrier phase): PPP uses the broadcast ionosphere model, about a metre.
No broadcast ephemerides yet: if the correction stream does not carry them, switch on the ephemeris stream (Setup > Receiver connection).
No SSR corrections in this stream yet: PPP needs a Galileo HAS or IGS SSRA… mountpoint (Setup > NTRIP relay).
This stream sends base station data for RTK, which PPP does not use: set Corrections to RTK (base) in Setup > Receiver connection, or choose a Galileo HAS / SSR stream.
Switch the NTRIP relay on (caster and mountpoint in Setup) for RTK; until then the phone gives a standalone position.

No broadcast ephemerides from the caster yet (RTCM 1019/1020/1045/1046/1042), and the phone needs them to compute satellite positions. Many network streams (VRS, nearest base) leave them out: switch on the ephemeris stream (Setup > Receiver connection).
No carrier phase from this phone at the moment: RTK cannot fix (code-only phone, or power saving still on). The position stays at metre level.
This stream sends PPP corrections (SSR), not base station data: set Corrections to PPP (HAS / SSR) in Setup > Receiver connection, or choose an RTK mountpoint.
Signals reach the phone by reflection (code residuals %1$s): the position can be off by metres or more, whatever accuracy RTK claims. Move to open sky, away from walls, cars and your body.
Weak signals: the engine also uses those down to %1$d dB-Hz
Weak signals: the engine uses all of them, even the weakest

Recording saves to files. Each session keeps the complete NMEA stream (raw.nmea, replayable in u-center) and a CSV of fixes with accuracy, filtered by the minimum fix and interval above. Export tracks as GPX or KML.
No points yet: use Mark point, or average one with Tools > Survey point.
RINEX %1$.1f kB · GnssLog %2$.1f kB · RTCM %3$.1f kB

Replay plays a session back as the source, so Live, Map, the tools and the position history work on it. NMEA sessions play as recorded; phone raw sessions (RINEX + RTCM) go through phone RTK again with the current settings.
Tap a point for its distance and bearing.
Asking the caster for its sourcetable…
Waiting for you to allow USB access.
Connect the receiver over USB (data port, OTG cable) or Bluetooth, or choose NMEA over TCP, in Setup. To try the app without hardware, choose the simulator.
No sentences of this type yet.
The receiver\'s sentences as they arrive, without saving a file. Filter by type, pause to read, copy or share what is shown. To keep a complete record, use Recording above.
This phone has no GNSS receiver: connect an external one

This phone has no GNSS (satellite positioning) receiver of its own. PocketGNSS is only useful with an external GNSS receiver connected over USB, Bluetooth or the network; the phone source and the phone raw GNSS tools are not available.
Shown while the app records, sends corrections or publishes the position with the screen off.
Changes to the caster, mountpoint, user name or password are saved to the selected profile at once.
Profile name (e.g. Metrica VRS, EOS base)
Passwords are encrypted with a key kept in the phone\'s Android Keystore; they are not backed up and never leave this phone except to the caster you choose.
Turn off for older casters that only speak version 1
Not a raster MBTiles file (PNG / JPEG / WebP tiles).

Map tiles you have viewed are kept on the phone and shown without a connection. Look over your fields once with signal, at the zoom you work at. Bulk downloading of the online maps is not allowed by their providers.
Your own map works fully offline: a raster MBTiles file, e.g. a drone orthophoto or a national orthophoto / topographic map exported from QGIS (Generate XYZ tiles, MBTiles) or gdal_translate.
Show own map over the base map
Active: other apps now get the receiver\'s position.
Could not start the mock location provider.
Other apps (AGENSO, field mapping, GIS) use the RTK position. Select PocketGNSS once in Developer options > Select mock location app.
Not allowed yet: select PocketGNSS in Developer options > Select mock location app, then Retry.
Not available with the phone as the source: publishing a mock location would replace the phone\'s own GNSS provider, and its measurements with it.
Off: PCs on the same network can connect too
Receive the high-precision position that PocketGNSS computes.
Not fixed yet: decimetres to metres
PPP, no base: decimetres to ~1 m
A photo is kept with the point and exported in KMZ (photos in the balloons); CSV, GeoJSON and shapefile name the file.
Phase resets or gaps were seen: power saving (duty cycling) may still be on, or the sky view is poor.
switched off by the app (full tracking)
turn on Developer options > Force full GNSS measurements
Phone RTK needs raw measurements with carrier phase, ideally on two bands (L1 + L5/E5a). Phones differ widely, so test each model outdoors under open sky.

RTKLIB (demo5): convert base.rtcm3 to RINEX with RTKCONV (it also gives the broadcast ephemeris), then RTKPOST with raw.obs as rover, the converted file as base, kinematic or static, combined, \"Time interpolation of base station data\" on and the base position from the RTCM 1005/1006 (or the surveyed coordinates). MATLAB: ProcessGnssMeasScript from Google\'s GNSS Measurement Tools reads the GnssLog file directly.

Static session of 20–30 minutes on a surveyed point, phone flat and still. Writes RINEX 3.04 observations, the same data in GnssLogger format (for Google\'s MATLAB GNSS Measurement Tools) and, from the caster set in Setup > NTRIP relay, the RTCM base stream at the same time. The caster gets the phone\'s position (GGA) when it needs one.
Set a caster and mountpoint in Setup > NTRIP relay first
Saved: share the files from Log > Sessions (RINEX, GnssLog, RTCM or all as ZIP).
Start outdoors with a clear sky view and the phone still for one to two minutes. Code = share of signals with a usable pseudorange; Phase = share with valid carrier phase.
Code only (no usable carrier phase): sub-metre at best with corrections (DGNSS), not RTK.
Carrier phase on L1 and L5/E5a: the best case for phone RTK.
Carrier phase on L1/E1: RTK float is possible; a fixed solution needs a short baseline and a long static session.
No raw measurements: this phone gives positions only. Phone RTK is not possible; use an external receiver.
Collecting… (keep the phone still under open sky)

Three boards: ESP32, LTE modem with nano-SIM (and SD card slot), u-blox F9x. The receiver\'s own NTRIP client gets corrections over the mobile network (data-only SIM, 4G/LTE recommended) or, if set, over Wi-Fi. Power on the middle micro-USB. D3.5: ~60 s from power-up to RTK data, re-connects in 16–25 s.
Choose the receiver version in Setup to see how it gets RTK corrections.

Two boards: ESP32 and u-blox F9x, no modem or SD slot. The receiver\'s own NTRIP client gets corrections only through a Wi-Fi access point (a field router, a mobile-broadband router or this phone\'s hotspot); anywhere with mobile coverage, the phone can also relay them over Bluetooth or USB (NTRIP relay). D3.5: fastest re-connection and ~99 % RTK availability over a fibre-fed router.

The upper (data) port is the ESP32\'s serial bridge at 115200 bd, as validated in D3.5. Automatic tries 115200 first, then 9600 and higher rates. The bottom port (u-blox chip, not normally used) ignores this.
Tap Connect to allow Bluetooth access, then come back here.
The receiver\'s adapter is named BTU-ESPrtk : <ID> (Tools > Receiver settings, section 10). Do not change its type or name on the receiver.
No paired devices. Pair the receiver first.

The phone fetches the corrections over its mobile data, sends the receiver\'s GGA to the caster (needed by VRS / network services such as Metrica) and forwards the RTCM stream to the receiver over Bluetooth or USB. This gives the compact AgriBIT receiver (no SIM board) RTK anywhere with mobile coverage, and works the same with any other RTK receiver that accepts RTCM 3 on its USB or Bluetooth link (u-blox F9P/F9R boards, survey receivers). With the phone as the source (Phone RTK) it feeds the phone\'s own RTK engine instead. Not needed when the receiver reaches the service itself over Wi-Fi or its own SIM. Switch it on from Live or Tools > Corrections.
Carrier phase is patchy on this phone: a fix must hold 10 epochs with a higher ratio before it is shown.
Learning: after about 10 minutes of Phone RTK the engine is tuned to what this phone delivers.
This phone rarely has enough carrier phase to fix: ambiguity fixing is off, so it reports honest float / code solutions instead of false fixes.
This phone delivers usable carrier phase: standard settings.
%1$.0f min · %2$.1f sats with phase · enough to fix %3$.0f %% · %4$.2f slips / sat-min
Changes take effect at the next Connect / Reconnect.

The phone\'s raw GNSS measurements are processed with the caster\'s corrections (RTKLIB demo5 on the phone): switch the NTRIP relay on. What a phone reaches depends on its chip and antenna, from decimetres (L1 only) to centimetres (L1 + L5 with carrier phase); without corrections it gives a standalone position. Off: Android\'s location only.
Not available: the RTK engine is not built for this phone\'s processor.

PPP needs no base station and no subscription: the NTRIP relay connects to a stream of satellite orbit, clock and code-bias corrections (SSR) and the phone\'s raw measurements are processed on their own. Galileo HAS is free from the EU after registration with the European GNSS Service Centre (gsc-europa.eu, HAS Internet Data Distribution); IGS real-time streams named SSRA… (free registration) work too. Expect decimetres to about a metre on a dual-frequency phone after 20–30 minutes under open sky, about a metre on L1-only phones. There is no ambiguity fixing, so not centimetres.
Streams named SSRC… refer orbits to the satellites\' centre of mass, which PocketGNSS does not use: choose Galileo HAS or an SSRA… stream (antenna phase centre).
Used to find the receiver\'s hotspot (ESPrtk : <ID>, ID shown on its LCD) and to show its login (RTKrover + device number).

One tap sets what worked best in tests: RTK with a base station (not PPP), moving mode, tuning to this phone, your Metrica account on MSM_VRS and the BCEP00BKG0 ephemeris stream with your BKG account. Saved accounts stay as they are.
No saved BKG account (igs-ip.net or euref-ip.net, free registration) for the ephemeris stream: add one under NTRIP relay, then tap Recommended again.
No saved RTK caster account (e.g. Metrica SmartNet): add one under NTRIP relay, then tap Recommended again.
Off: the simulated receiver stays on SBAS unless the phone\'s NTRIP client sends RTCM
Arrow relative to your direction of travel
No points to stake out: save points first (Survey point or Mark point).
Arrow relative to north (move to use the direction of travel)
Sentences per second; GSA and GSV send several per epoch, so the navigation rate is the GGA or RMC figure. AgriBIT spec: 1, 5, 10 or 20 Hz (D3.5 GNSS-test-08 confirmed 20 Hz at 115200 bd).
Only fixes at least this good are averaged; the others are counted as rejected.
At least two accepted fixes are needed.
Enter a known coordinate (for example from the EOS Arrow Gold or a survey marker) to see the bias and RMS error against it, as in the AgriBIT validation tests.
Errors, warnings and events, to find out what happened
NTRIP relay through the phone, RTCM messages, base distance, mountpoints
Walk or drive round a field, or mark its corners: area, perimeter, KML / SHP export
A-B lines, curves and headland passes at the implement width, with a lightbar and coverage map
Every computed position with its method and accuracy; reported vs actual scatter; CSV log
Choose messages, ports and rate (1–20 Hz) on the u-blox chip, like u-center
What this phone\'s chip delivers for RTK; record RINEX + RTCM for post-processing
Guide to a saved point to the centimetre
Message rates, gaps, errors and the raw NMEA console

Cold, warm and hot start to fix, float and RTK fixed
Open the receiver\'s own web server (ESPrtk) on its Wi-Fi hotspot
Every tool also works with the simulator, so you can try it before using the receiver in the field.
Connect a receiver or the simulator first.
Allow USB access to the receiver

No corrections reach the receiver. Check on its LCD the mobile signal bars and the NTRIP data mark; check the SIM (data enabled, no PIN) and APN in section 16, the caster in section 7; allow about a minute after power-up.
No corrections reach the receiver. Choose the receiver version in Setup for what to check, or send corrections from the phone (Setup > NTRIP).

No corrections reach the receiver. It needs a Wi-Fi access point in range (router or this phone\'s hotspot, with the SSID and password set in section 4) and the caster in section 7 — or switch on the NTRIP relay through the phone.
Your link may not pass commands to the u-blox chip: choose Power-cycle, then unplug and re-plug the receiver\'s power (middle port). Cold / warm / hot need the bottom (u-blox) USB port.
Cold, warm and hot restart the GNSS with UBX CFG-RST (the link stays up). Power-cycle: start, then unplug and re-plug the receiver\'s power.
AgriBIT spec: cold start < 60 s, re-acquisition 1 s. D3.5 measured 55–60 s to RTK data over LTE and 25–30 s more to RTK fixed.
Same result as the u-center steps in the receiver guide: one CFG-VALSET per group, each acknowledged by the receiver. Keep GGA and RMC on for AGENSO\'s apps.
Connected to the u-blox chip directly: configuration commands reach it.
GGA and RMC are needed by most apps (AGENSO\'s included) and by this one.
No answer: this link does not pass UBX to the u-blox chip. Connect the bottom micro-USB port (u-blox chip).
RAM + battery-backed RAM + Flash, like u-center\'s Save config. Off: until the next power-down.
The phone\'s own GNSS chip cannot be configured from here; connect the RFSAT receiver.
u-blox ports to configure. The receiver guide sets I2C, UART1, USB and SPI; UART1 feeds the ESP32 (Bluetooth and the receiver\'s own logging).
Navigation rate. 20 Hz needs 115200 bd or more and only GGA/RMC; GSV is sent once per second.

Connected through the ESP32 (upper USB port or Bluetooth): configuration works only if its firmware passes UBX through. If nothing is confirmed, connect the bottom micro-USB port (the u-blox chip itself, as u-center does).
Which receiver do you have? The larger one has a third board with a SIM card (LTE modem) and gets RTK corrections over the mobile network; the compact one has no modem and gets them over Wi-Fi.
How this receiver reaches the RTK service
User name and password are the same: RTKrover followed by the device number written on the case (for example RTKrover01). Do not change them on the receiver.
Always Logout (and wait for the confirmation) before powering down or resetting the receiver.
Where there is a Wi-Fi router, section 4 can use Wi-Fi instead (1 AP Wi-Fi, SSID and password), which re-connects faster.

LTE version: insert a data-only nano-SIM (4G/LTE; PIN disabled) in the modem board. In section 4 choose Internet via Quectel BG96; in section 16 enter the operator\'s APN, user and password (a single space for empty fields). Send and check the status window.
Not connected to any Wi-Fi: connect to ESPrtk : <ID> in Android Wi-Fi settings first
Receiver hotspot not found. Is the LCD showing the hotspot screen?
The phone\'s NTRIP client pauses while this screen is open: the hotspot has no internet.

Both versions: in section 7 NTRIP Client enter the caster address, port, user, password and mountpoint of your RTK service (e.g. METRICA / HxGN SmartNet). The receiver then corrects its position itself; this app only reads it.
3 Action Planning: device mode 5/17 NTRIP_Rover, NMEA to Bluetooth and UART0. Do not modify.
10 Bluetooth: Bluetooth Classic BTU. Do not change type or name.
Do not modify: Ublox, Navspark, System tabs; 1 Create new profile; 9 UART Configure; 17–20 Stream manager.
16 GSM-2G-3G-4G-LTE (LTE version): APN, user and password of the SIM\'s operator (a single space for empty fields).
4 Internet – RTK online: Quectel BG96 with the SIM, or Wi-Fi to a router (1 AP Wi-Fi, SSID and password; default SSID RFSAT).
4 Internet – RTK online: Wi-Fi only (1 AP Wi-Fi, SSID and password of the router or phone hotspot). The compact version has no modem: do not select Quectel BG96.

14 SD Card Logger (LTE version, SD slot on the modem board): NMEA logging to the receiver\'s own SD card.
The receiver at %1$s uses its own (self-signed) certificate. Continue to its settings page?
1. Hold the top button of the receiver for 5 seconds, until the LCD shows the Wi-Fi hotspot screen.
2. Tap Join: Android asks to connect to ESPrtk : %1$s.
3. The receiver\'s settings open at 192.168.4.1. Log in, change what you need, press Send and check the status window.

Changes are your responsibility. Never create a new profile and never change the device type or reset options: this can make the receiver unusable until RFSAT reconfigures it. If login fails, use the HARD reset (pin under the case, marked R).

No router in the field? Turn on this phone\'s mobile hotspot with the same SSID and password as in section 4: the receiver then reaches the RTK service through the phone\'s mobile data. Many phones cannot run a hotspot while joined to the receiver\'s own Wi-Fi, so finish these settings first.

Wi-Fi version: in section 4 choose Internet via Wi-Fi, Number Access Point 1 AP Wi-Fi, and the SSID and password of the router in the field (default RFSAT); keep Smart Scan on. Send and check the status window.
